evidence: Cic. Att. 14.1.1; Off. 1.149 (Lewis & Short, s.v. summa)
terms.comment: Sums up what has been said: “all in all, in a word”. Common in Cicero’s letters and in talk (Petronius’ freedmen).

evidence: Cic. Q. Fr. 2.16.3: in summā quattuor sententiīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of a count: “in all”. In post-Augustan prose also “at last”.
“Altogether, at all”; with numbers “in all, only”. For the adjective (“the overall picture”) use tōtus or ūniversus (see whole).

phrases.latin: ad summam, quotīdiē mē solēbam ad illum mētīrī
phrases.english: in short, I used to measure myself against it every day
All in all, we had a good time.
